reason: The passage names several characters who do not function as leaders. Most significantly, Aun/On (בן־ פֶּלֶת), son of Peleth, is explicitly named in the opening verse ('וַיִּקַּח קֹרַח... וְא֥וֹן בֶּן־ פֶּ֖לֶת') as part of the rebellion, but then never appears again in the narrative and takes no active role. He neither speaks nor leads. While Korah, Dathan, and Abiram do act as rebel leaders, and Moses, Aaron, and Eleazar are legitimate institutional leaders, On is a named character who is merely a listed participant without leadership agency or function.
